quick.summary: Why we argue with criticism, and three steps to hear it instead.

beats.line: My lead said my report was confusing. Why did I argue straight away?
Criticism feels like a threat. Defending comes on its own.
So what do I do, just agree?
No. Just don’t decide yet. Try three steps.
First, say thanks. It buys you a calm second.
Second, ask one question to understand it.
Isn’t thanking them for criticism a bit fake?
You’re thanking them for telling you. That part is real.
Third, decide later what to change.
Thanks. Which part lost you first?
Now you get the useful detail, not a debate.

quiz.question: Someone says your work was confusing. What is the best first response?
options: Thanks. Which part lost you first?
That is because the brief changed.
Okay, I will redo all of it.
quiz.explanation: It thanks them and asks for the detail you need, without defending or giving in.

quiz.question: Taking feedback well means agreeing with all of it on the spot.
quiz.explanation: You can thank them, ask to understand, and decide later what to change.
